message.content:
`contenteditable` is a **boolean** attribute in HTML.  
Its allowed values are:

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `"true"`   | The element is editable. |
| `"false"`  | The element is not editable. |
| `"inherit"`| The element inherits the value from its parent (default). |

Anything else – including `"plaintext-only"` – is **not part of the official specification**. Some libraries or custom frameworks may accept `"plaintext-only"` as an extension, but browsers will ignore it and fall back to the default behavior.

So, if you need to support standard‑compliant markup, you cannot convert `"plaintext-only"` into a valid boolean string for `contenteditable`. You would have to decide how you want to interpret that value yourself (e.g., treat it as `"false"` or ignore it) and then apply the corresponding standard value (`"true"`, `"false"`, or `"inherit"`).
